name: Nicaragua

findings.financier: Zhengzhou Coal Mining Machinery Group Co., Ltd. (ZMJ), PRC
findings.summary: Nicaragua signed two credit agreements with Chinese firm ZMJ, 612m yuan (about US$84.2m), funding a 4G/5G Digital Connectivity Project executed by state utility ENATREL; the National Assembly ratified them in June 2025.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole left null: the controller rule needs the equipment vendor, and no source names the RAN/core vendor (Huawei/ZTE not mentioned). ZMJ, a coal-machinery firm, is the PRC lender and contracted supplier, likely acting as a financing/EPC vehicle; recorded as financier. A PRC vendor is plausible but unconfirmed. Value: US$84.2m as stated by Mobile Time/DPL; EFE (citing La Gaceta) gives US$85.7m at authorisation stage. Tier 3 = signed and ratified loan/supply agreements; disbursement and construction not confirmed. Phase 1 Managua and Ciudad Sandino, phase 2 cities in 14 departments; sources say it would create a state-owned third mobile operator.

findings.summary: Nicaragua's government announced a Digital Transformation and 5G Technologies Plan with Huawei in late 2023; in April 2025 Ortega met Huawei's Latin America president with Telcor and ENATREL heads to review joint projects and expand telecom cooperation.
findings.analyst_inference: Statement/plan level only (tier 1); no contract, value or deployment found. Accounts differ: La Prensa and Bloomberg Línea say the plan was signed/announced Nov 2023, while AFP (Dec 2023) described Nicaragua as still seeking a 5G plan with Huawei. All details trace to Nicaraguan government statements. No S1/S2 source opened, so not corroborated. Whether this plan underlies the ENATREL 4G/5G project (NIC-001) is not established.

findings.summary: The state National Council of Universities inaugurated a Managua data centre for the national education information system, built in collaboration with Huawei, with investment of over 120m córdobas (about US$3.2m); specifications were not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Facility owner-operator is the state CNU, so pole domestic. Huawei's role (IT/network equipment vendor vs builder) is unspecified; if it supplied the servers/network gear, an IT-layer PRC finding would also apply, but this is not confirmed so it is not coded. Small facility (~US$3.2m), not an AI campus. Both items are DCD (same host) relaying a TN8 report, so not corroborated. Value is DCD's conversion, not put in value fields.

findings.summary: Nicaragua's police chief and China's Minister of Public Security signed a security cooperation agreement at a September 2024 forum in Lianyungang, covering officer training and provision of police techniques and technologies against terrorism, drug trafficking and cybercrime.
findings.analyst_inference: Non-binding cooperation agreement (tier 1); no named surveillance vendor, system or procurement found. Agreement content relayed from a state press release (origin government unspecified). Opposition claims of a Managua surveillance centre using Chinese technology are unverified and not coded.
